method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; three seat modules over one small date module; two regulative rules (the s 64(5), (7) deadlines with the s 90 permission after them, as PARTY ... MUST ... WITHIN ... HENCE ... ROR ... LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE; the s 100 record-keeping duty, as SHANT ... WITHIN ... LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE), each with seat questions that read plain dates; no REFUSE (a case the Act does not speak to answers a `not covered` constructor, asserted); every opinion, belief or satisfaction of a coroner, the Chief Coroner, the Attorney-General or the Supreme Court asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Coroners Act 1997 (ACT), A1997-57, Republication No 51 (R51), effective 2026-09-05, ACT Legislation Register, retrieved 2026-11-06, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/A1997-57.txt. No instrument brought in: the regulation s 68A(2) would prescribe, the Court Procedures Rules 2006 schedule 4 (s 98) and the Legislation Act 2001 (ss 133, 151, 169, 171) are not deposited.

checks.command: l4 run coroners-dates.l4 ; l4 run coroners-family.l4 ; l4 run coroners-witness.l4 ; l4 run coroners-owner.l4 ; l4 run coroners-cases-family.l4 ; l4 run coroners-cases-witness.l4 ; l4 run coroners-cases-owner.l4
checks.result: 236 assertions satisfied (family 151, witness 61, owner 24), 0 errors, 0 warnings on all seven files; 2 #TRACEs as their expect lines say (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A breached DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the rules are asserted through CONSIDER ... WHEN FULFILLED and one breach of each is #TRACEd.

seats: a member of the deceased's immediate family (or their representative) -- coroners-family.l4

a witness: a person summoned or asked to give evidence, documents or information, including a person the coroner may criticise, the treating doctor, and the person in charge of the records -- coroners-witness.l4
the owner or occupier of property damaged by fire, or of a place searched or made a coronial investigation scene -- coroners-owner.l4
